title: Latency-aware attention pipeline allocator + microfusion kernel for short-prefix workloads
author: Ariana Park
description:
Motivation: production workloads show a bimodal distribution: many short prefix requests (<=64 tokens, low throughput sensitivity) and long-context streaming requests. The existing kernel selection and batching policies favor throughput which increases p99 latency for short requests and causes cold-KV stalls when workloads switch. This PR introduces a latency-aware pipeline allocator and a lightweight microfusion attention kernel optimized for short sequences and low-queue latency.

What this PR does (summary): introduces a new scheduler 'latency-pipeline-allocator' that tags incoming requests by estimated criticality (short-prefix vs streaming), favors immediate dispatch for latency-critical requests, and pins them to a new microfusion kernel variant (attn_microfusion_light) that merges QK and attention reduction with a small on-chip scratch allocation to avoid spilling small KV windows. Adds proactive KV pre-warm policy for rollouts where the same conversation hits the model repeatedly. Integrates allocator with continuous batching: a fast-path that flushes batches early if any latency-critical request is present, preserving batching for throughput paths.

Implementation notes: allocator lives in runtime/scheduler/latency_allocator.cc, microfusion kernel is in runtime/kernels/microfusion_light.cu with `FlashLite`-compatible entrypoints, and a thin selection shim in runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc. New config flags: runtime.latency_allocator.enabled (bool), runtime.latency_allocator.short_threshold (tokens), runtime.kv.prewarm.window_ms. Backwards-compatible: default disabled; selector falls back to existing fusion kernels when microfusion not available for a device.

Benchmarks: see benchmarks/latency_allocator/README.md added in this PR. In mixed synthetic workloads (50% short-prefix 50% long streaming) on A100s: p50 unchanged, p95 improved 9-12%, p99 improved 18-22% for short-prefix path; overall token throughput decreased ~3% in worst-case when allocator forced early flushes, but cost-per-token improved for latency-sensitive flows because fewer timeouts and retries occurred.

Testing: unit tests for kernel selector and allocator heuristics added under runtime/scheduler/tests. CI includes microbench harness that runs short sequence latency tests on small GPUs (can be skipped on PR runners).

Rollout plan: opt-in behind runtime.latency_allocator.enabled. Initial rollout to small canary fleet (regional tag: canary-latency) with 10% traffic, monitor cost, p99 latency, KV miss rates. If regressions detected fallback to default scheduler automatically via runtime.policy.fallback_on_regression.

Notes on correctness: microfusion_light implements FP16 accumulation with the same numeric pipeline as other fused kernels; additional unit tests compare outputs (max abs diff < 1e-3) on representative inputs.

Related: complements ENG-4010 (continuous batching eviction policies) and should be evaluated alongside pr-122500 and the KV warmup pilot (no direct overlap with their code paths).
commits:
6 commits:
- Add latency-aware pipeline allocator (runtime/scheduler)
- Implement microfusion_light kernel (runtime/kernels)
- Kernel selector shim and device capability checks
- KV pre-warm policy and metrics hooks
- Add unit and integration tests + benchmark harness
- Docs: README and rollout notes
performance_summary: Mixed workload (50/50 short/long) on A100: p50 ~0% change, p95 -9% to -12% (latency path), p99 -18% to -22% (latency path). Overall tokens/sec -3% worst-case. KV miss rate for short recency flows reduced by ~35% due to pre-warm policy.
review_comments: Samir Gupta (review): Looks good overall; please add guard rails so the allocator cannot starve throughput-critical batches. Request: add a max_early_flush_rate config and a unit test for it.
Author (Ariana Park): Added max_early_flush_rate (default 0.2) and tests to verify throughput starvation doesn't happen. See allocator_test.cc commit 4.

Eva Chen (review): Microfusion kernel uses a custom scratch allocator; ensure CUDA multi-stream safety and add comments about stream-bound allocations. Also request microbench numbers for T4 for cost estimations.
Author: Added stream-safety notes and changed allocator to rely on per-stream arena; included additional T4 microbench results in benchmarks/latency_allocator/README.md.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after small nit: rename runtime.kv.prewarm.window_ms -> runtime.kv.prewarm.window_ms_hint for clarity.
Author: Renamed flag and updated docs.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (merge commit 0f3a2b) - commit message consolidated: "Add latency-aware pipeline allocator and microfusion_light kernel; KV prewarm and tests."
release_notes: Introduce latency-aware pipeline allocator and a microfusion attention kernel optimized for short-prefix workloads. Opt-in via runtime.latency_allocator.enabled. Improves p99 latency for short requests by up to ~22% in mixed workloads. (Performance opt-in behind config.)
